旧[[県社]] |創建 = （伝）[[崇神天皇]]48年 |本殿 = |別名 = |札所等 = |例祭 = [[11月18日]]-[[11月26日|26日]] |神事 = |地図={{Location map|Japan Tochigi|label=大神神社|caption=|coordinates= {{coord2|36|24|21.30|N|139|46|55.76|E|}} |position=top|width=200|mark=Shinto torii icon vermillion.svg|marksize=20|float=center }}}} [[ファイル:Oomiwa-jinja (tochigishi) ichinotorii.JPG|thumb|200px|一の鳥居]] '''大神神社'''（おおみわじんじゃ）は、[[栃木県]][[栃木市]][[惣社町 (栃木市)|惣社町]]にある[[神社]]。[[式内社]]（小）[[論社]]、[[下野国]][[総社]]。[[近代社格制度|旧社格]]は[[県社]]。古くは「下野惣社大明神」「惣社六所大明神」「室八島惣社大明神」などの別称があった。 律令時代には神社の南約2kmに国府が置かれ、大神神社は国府の惣社となり、この地（惣社）の地名の由来にもなっている{{Cite web |url=https://www.city.tochigi.lg.jp/uploaded/attachment/55689.pdf|title=第2章 栃木市の維持向上すべき歴史的風致|website=栃木市|accessdate=2024-11-11|page=177}}。 [[松尾芭蕉]]『[[奥の細道]]』に登場する境内の「'''室の八嶋'''」が知られている。 == 祭神 == '''主祭神''' * '''倭大物主櫛𤭖玉命''' （やまとおおものぬしくしみかたまのみこと）祭神は神社由緒書に従う。 *: 『[[出雲国造神賀詞]]』では[[大物主|大物主神]]を指す。[[大神神社]]（[[奈良県]][[桜井市]]）からの分霊。 [[崇神天皇]]が[[天変地異]]や[[疫病]]の流行に悩んでいると、夢に大物主が現れ、「こは我が心ぞ。意富多多泥古（[[大田田根子]]）をもちて、我が御魂を祭らしむれば、神の気起こらず、国安らかに平らぎなむ」と告げた。天皇は早速、[[活玉依毘売]]の末裔とされる[[意富多多泥古]]を捜し出し、[[三輪山]]で祭祀を行わせたところ、天変地異も疫病も収まったという。これが現在の大神神社である。『[[日本書紀]]』では、崇神天皇が大物主から夢で直接に[[神託]]を得るまでの[[亀卜]]や[[沐浴]][[物忌み|斎戒]]、宮殿内部の[[祓|潔浄]]と言った[[祭祀]]の過程と内容が詳細に記され、天変地異が収まった翌年に大神神社に奉る酒の管掌に[[高橋神社|高橋邑]]の人活日が任命されている。 '''配祀神''' * [[コノハナノサクヤビメ|木花咲耶姫命]] （このはなさくやひめのみこと） * [[ニニギ|瓊々杵命]] （ににぎのみこと） - 木花咲耶姫命の夫神 * [[オオヤマツミ|大山祇命]] （おおやまつみのみこと） - 木花咲耶姫命の父 * [[ホオリ|彦火々出見命]] （ひこほほでみのみこと） - 木花咲耶姫命の子。火遠理命に同じ == 歴史 == === 創建 === 社伝では、[[崇神天皇]]の時代に[[豊城入彦命]]（崇神天皇[[皇子]]）が東国平定の折に戦勝と人心平安を祈願し、当時から広く名を知られた'''室の八嶋'''（むろのやしま、室の八島とも記す）に、崇神天皇が都とした[[大和国]][[磯城瑞籬宮]]（現在の[[奈良県]][[桜井市]]金屋）に座した大三輪大神（[[大神神社]]）を勧請したのが創建とされている神社由緒書。。 === 概史 === [[平安時代]]中期の『[[延喜式神名帳]]』には「下野国[[都賀郡]] 大神社」の記載があるが、当社をそれにあてる説がありその[[論社]]とされている他の論社として[[太平山神社]]（栃木県栃木市[[平井町 (栃木市)|平井町]]）がある。。 また、[[古代]]の[[国司]]は各国内の全ての神社を一宮から順に巡拝していたが、これを効率化するため、各国の[[国府]]近くに国内の神を合祀した[[総社]]を設け、まとめて祭祀を行うようになった。当社はそのうちの[[下野国]]の総社にあたるとされる。当社の南方約2.8kmの地には[[下野国庁跡]]も発掘されている。 [[承平天慶の乱#平将門の乱|平将門の乱]]により被害を受けたが、[[藤原秀郷]]らの寄進により再建され、[[室町時代]]まで社殿は広く立派であったと伝える。しかし[[戦国時代 (日本)|戦国時代]]に、[[皆川広照]]の残兵が当社に篭り、[[北条氏直]]の軍勢が火を放ったために焼失し、荒廃した。その後、[[徳川家光]]による社領30石と松の苗1万本の寄進などにより、[[1682年]]（[[天和 (日本)|天和]]2年）に現在の形へと復興したという。 しかしながら、実際には[[明治|明治時代]]より以前の史料で当社を明確に「大神（おおみわ）」または「大三輪」と呼んだものは発見されていない。「実際のところは、[[都]]から遣わされた[[国司]]が大和国の[[大神神社]]（大三輪神社）を別の場所で祀っていて、これが下野惣社大明神に合祀され同化した」といった説境内説明板。もあるなど、その歴史は必ずしも詳らかとは言い難い。 [[明治維新]]後、明治6年に[[近代社格制度]]において[[郷社]]に列し、明治40年に神饌幣帛料共進神社に指定、明治44年に[[県社]]に昇格した。[[1924年]]（[[大正]]13年）に社殿の大改修、[[1993年]]（[[平成]]5年）に室の八嶋の大改修などが行われて現在に至っている。なお、古来より[[社家]][[宮司|大宮司]]は國保家が代々世襲していた。 === 神階 === * [[元慶]]4年（[[880年]]）8月29日、従五位下から正五位上 （『[[日本三代実録]]』） - 表記は「三和神」で、当社にあてる説がある『栃木県の地名』大神神社項。 == 境内 == === 社殿 === ファイル:Oomiwa-jinja (tochigishi) honden.JPG|本殿 ファイル:Oomiwa-jinja (tochigishi) haiden.JPG|拝殿 ファイル:Oomiwa-jinja (tochigishi) kaguraden.JPG|神楽殿 === 境内林 === 大神神社の境内林を中心とする地域は、栃木県の惣社緑地環境保全地域となっている{{Cite web |url=https://www.pref.tochigi.lg.jp/d04/30jikannti/12souja.html|title=12 惣社（そうじゃ）緑地環境保全地域|website=栃木県 |accessdate=2024-11-11}}。 === 室の八嶋 === [[ファイル:Oomiwa-jinja (tochigishi) muronoyashima.JPG|thumb|200px|室の八嶋]] [[ファイル:TochigiOhmiwaShine2.JPG|thumb|200px|室の八嶋の前に建つ松尾芭蕉の句碑]] '''室の八嶋'''（むろのやしま）は、古来の和歌などに[[歌枕]]として見られる地名。当社境内の池中の島をその跡と伝える（ただし後世の付会とする説もある『大辞林』室の八島項（朝日新聞社コトバンクに[https://kotobank.jp/word/%E5%AE%A4%E3%81%AE%E5%85%AB%E5%B3%B6-642624 該当記事]）。）。[[奈良時代]]の昔から、[[歌枕]]として[[都]]にまでその名を知られ、『[[万葉集]]』や『[[古今和歌集]]』をはじめとする多くの[[和歌]]集などに登場する。 '''主な歌''' * いかでかは 思ひありとも 知らすべき 室の八嶋の 煙ならでは - [[藤原実方]]（『[[詞花和歌集]]』） * 人を思ふ 思ひを何に たとへまし 室の八島も 名のみ也けり - 源重之女（『[[続後拾遺和歌集]]』） * 煙たつ 室の八嶋に あらぬ身は こがれしことぞ くやしかりける - [[大江匡房]]（『[[新拾遺和歌集]]』） * いかにせん 室の八島に 宿もがな 恋の煙を 空にまがへん - [[藤原俊成]]（『[[長秋詠藻]]』） * 暮るる夜は 衛士のたく火を それと見よ 室の八島も 都ならねば - [[藤原定家]]（『[[新勅撰和歌集]]』） '''歌枕としての意味''' * [[木花咲耶姫命]]が一夜にして懐妊したためその貞操を証すべく、自ら火を放った室の中で三柱の[[神]]を産んだ、とされる[[神話]]の舞台。また転じて、[[竈]]（かまど）の[[煙]]（八嶋は竈の古語であるとの説もある）。 * [[思川 (栃木県)|思川]]の低湿地であることから、水煙や清水の沸く土地。 * これらが転じて、燃え上がる[[恋]]の炎に身を焼く煙。 * 糸遊（いとあそび、いとゆう）。煙が更に転じたものとも考えられるが、「[[陽炎]]{{要曖昧さ回避|date=2022年12月}}」「[[蜘蛛]]が糸を引いて飛ぶ」など作者の真意は様々で、定かではない。 当地を訪れたとされる[[松尾芭蕉]]と[[河合曾良|曾良]]は『[[奥の細道]]』に、室の八嶋の由緒などを曾良の言として記しているが、[[俳句]]は載せていない。しかし、後年曾良が著した『[[曾良旅日記#俳諧書留|俳諧書留]]」に、芭蕉の句として「いと遊に結びつきたるけふりかな」が記されており、これが当社の境内に句碑として建立されている。 [[1869年]]〈[[明治]]2〉3月、[[江戸時代|江戸後期]]の俳人である杲雲閣春峰が建立し、江戸後期に活躍した書家の萩原秋巌による筆とされる{{Cite web |title=とちぎいにしえの回廊｜文化財の歴史 |url=https://www.inishie.tochigi.jp/detail.html?course_id=5&id=0 |website=www.inishie.tochigi.jp |access-date=2024-02-22}}。 現在見られる「室の八嶋」は、[[杉]]木立の中の掘割に、小さな祠を戴く8つの小[[島]]がある、およそ800坪ほどの[[庭園]]状の場所であり、水煙や[[湧き水]]などは観られない。8つの祠には、[[筑波山神社|筑波]]・[[天満宮|天満]]・[[鹿島神宮|鹿嶋]]・[[雷電神社|雷電]]・[[富士山本宮浅間大社|浅間]]・[[熊野大社|熊野]]・[[二荒山神社|二荒山]]・[[香取神宮|香取]]の各名神が祀られている。 == 摂末社 == [[ファイル:Oomiwa-jinja (tochigishi) jingu.JPG|thumb|200px|神宮
本社の相殿を祀る。]] 境内社は以下の15社。 {{div col}} * 神宮 * 護国神社 * 福神神社 * 大杉神社 * 祖霊社 * 左門神社 * 右門神社 {{div col end}} '''室の八嶋''' {{div col}} * 浅間神社 * 二荒山神社 * 筑波神社 * 雷電神社 * 香取神社 * 鹿島神社 * 熊野神社 * 天満宮 {{div col end}} == 祭事 == * 元旦祭 （[[1月1日]]）祭事は[http://kir579053.kir.jp/jinjyacyo/?p=538 大神神社]（栃木県神社庁）参照。 * 初詣・新春祈願祭 （1月中） * 節分祭・追儺式 （[[2月3日]]） * 祈年祭 （[[2月25日]]） * 鎮花祭 （3月上旬） * '''春季例大祭''' （[[4月16日]]） - 流鏑馬を催行 * 初申祭 （5月初申の日） * 大祓 （[[6月30日]]） * 八島祭 （[[8月1日]]） * 大杉祭・風祭 （8月中旬） * 七五三詣り （[[11月15日]]） * '''秋季例大祭（御鉾祭）''' （[[11月18日]]-[[11月24日|24日]]頃） == 文化財 == === 栃木市指定無形民俗文化財 === * 大神神社の神楽 - 昭和39年5月19日指定 * 大神神社の鉾祭 - 昭和39年5月19日指定 === 史跡 === * 栃木市指定史跡「下野惣社（室の八嶋）」 - 昭和43年2月16日指定 == 現地情報 == '''所在地''' * [[栃木県]][[栃木市]][[惣社町 (栃木市)|惣社町]]477 '''交通アクセス''' * [[東武鉄道]][[東武宇都宮線|宇都宮線]] [[野州大塚駅]] （徒歩約15分） '''周辺''' * [[下野国庁跡]] - 南方約2.8km == 脚注 == {{脚注ヘルプ}} {{reflist}} == 参考文献 == * 『大神神社概要』（神社由緒書） * 『日本歴史地名体系 栃木県の地名』（[[平凡社]]）栃木市 大神神社 == 関連項目 == * [[大神神社]] （[[奈良県]][[桜井市]]） == 外部リンク == * [http://www.kuranomachi.jp/spot/soja/omiwa/ 大神神社]（栃木市観光協会） * [http://kir579053.kir.jp/jinjyacyo/?p=538 大神神社]（栃木県神社庁） {{神道 横}} {{DEFAULTSORT:おおみわしんしやとちきし}} [[Category:栃木県の神社]] [[Category:栃木市の歴史]] [[Category:栃木市の建築物]] [[Category:下野国の式内社]] [[Category:総社]] [[Category:栃木県の旧県社]] [[Category:三輪神社]] [[Category:下野国|社0]]

revision.text:
{{Distinguish|Omiwa Shrine}}{{draft}} {{Infobox religious building | religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]] | image = Oomiwa-jinja (tochigishi) torii.JPG | deity = all the deities of its province | type = [[Sōja (Shinto)|Sōja shrine]] }} {{ill|Ōmiwa Jinja (Shimotsuke)|lt=Ōmiwa Jinja|ja|大神神社 (栃木市)}} is a [[Sōja (Shinto)|Sōja shrine]]. It enshrines all the [[kami]] of the shrines in [[Shimotsuke Province]] Ichinomiya and Soja are not the same thing but were sometimes combinedhttps://archive.ph/wip/XtZfZ {{nihongo|'''Sōja'''|総社|}} is a type of [[Shinto shrine]] where the ''[[kami]]'' of a region are grouped together into a single sanctuary. This "region" may refer to a ''[[shōen]]'', village or geographic area, but is more generally referred to a whole [[Provinces of Japan|province]]. The term is also occasionally called "'''sōsha'''". The ''sōja'' are usually located near the [[kokufu|provincial capital]] established in the [[Nara period]] under then ''[[ritsuryō]]'' system, and can either be a newly created shrine, or a designation for an existing shrine. The "sōja" can also be the "[[ichinomiya]]" of the province, which themselves are of great ritual importance.{{cite book |last1=Herbert |first1=Jean |title=Shinto:At the Fountain-head of Japan |date=2011 |publisher=Routledge |isbn=978-0-415-59348-9 |page=105}} Whenever a new [[Kokushi (official)|kokushi]] was appointed by the central government to govern a province, it was necessary for him to visit all of the sanctuaries of his province in order to complete the rites necessary for ceremonial inauguration. Grouping the ''kami'' into one location near the capital of the province greatly facilitated this duty,{{cite book |last1=Bocking |first1=Brian |title=A Popular Dictionary of Shinto |date=2016 |publisher=Routledge |isbn=978-1138979079}} The first mention of "sōja" appeared in the [[Heian period]], in the diary of Taira no Tokinori, dated March 9, 1099 in reference to the province of [[Inaba]]. {{cite book |last1=Hardacre |first1=Helen |title=Shinto: A History |date=2016 |publisher=Oxford University Press |isbn=978-0190621711}} The name "Sōja" is also found in place names such as the city of [[Sōja, Okayama| Sōja]] in [[Okayama Prefecture]]. ==Japanese content== {{Infobox Shinto shrine | name = Ōmiwa Jinja (Oomiwa Shrine) | image = [[File:Oomiwa-jinja (tochigishi) torii.JPG|280px]]
Torii | caption = | map_type = Japan Tochigi | coordinates = {{Coord|36|24|21.30|N|139|46|55.76|E|region:JP-09_type:landmark|display=inline,title|name=Ōmiwa Jinja}} | location = Sōja-chō 477, {{ill|Tochigi (city)|ja|栃木市|lt=Tochigi City}}, {{ill|Tochigi Prefecture|ja|栃木県|lt=Tochigi Prefecture}} | deity = Yamato-Ōmononushi-Kushi-mikatama no Mikoto | type = Shikinaisha (small), a disputed identification (ronsha), Sōja of Shimotsuke Province, Former Prefectural Shrine | founded = (Trad.) 48th year of Emperor Sujin’s reign | festival = November 18–26 }} '''Ōmiwa Jinja''' (大神神社, also romanized as Oomiwa Jinja) is a {{ill|Shinto shrine|ja|神社}} located in Sōja-chō, {{ill|Tochigi (city)|ja|栃木市|lt=Tochigi City}}, {{ill|Tochigi Prefecture|ja|栃木県|lt=Tochigi Prefecture}}, Japan. It is a possible match (ronsha) for a "Shikinaisha" (small) recorded in historical texts, and is known as the Sōja (total shrine) of Shimotsuke Province. Under the modern shrine rank system of the Meiji era, it was classified as a Prefectural Shrine. Historically, it was also known by other names such as "Shimotsuke Sōja Daimyōjin," "Sōja Rokusho Daimyōjin," and "Muroyashima Sōja Daimyōjin." During the Ritsuryō era, the provincial capital (kokufu) was located about 2 km south of the shrine. Ōmiwa Jinja served as the sōja of that kokufu, and the local place name “Sōja” is derived from this shrine.{{Cite web |url=https://www.city.tochigi.lg.jp/uploaded/attachment/55689.pdf|title=Chapter 2: Historical Scenery of Tochigi City to be Maintained and Improved |website=Tochigi City|accessdate=2024-11-11|page=177}} The shrine is also known for the "Muro no Yashima" (Muro no Yashima) mentioned in Matsuo Bashō’s famous travelogue, the "Oku no Hosomichi." == Deities Enshrined == '''Principal Deity:''' * *Yamato-Ōmononushi-Kushi-mikatama no Mikoto* (倭大物主櫛𤭖玉命)According to the shrine's official literature. : In the "Izumo no Kuni no Miyatsuko Kamuyogoto," this refers to Ōmononushi no Kami. The deity is said to be an offshoot of the Ōmiwa Jinja (大神神社) in Sakurai City, Nara Prefecture. During Emperor Sujin’s reign, suffering from natural disasters and plagues, the emperor had a dream in which the deity Ōmononushi appeared and gave instructions. Following them, a man named Ootataneko performed rites at Mount Miwa, resulting in the cessation of calamities and epidemics. This story is recorded in the "Nihon Shoki." '''Additional Deities (Aiadono-matsuri):''' * Kono-hanasakuya-hime (木花咲耶姫命) * Ninigi no Mikoto (瓊々杵命), husband of Kono-hanasakuya-hime * Ōyamatsumi no Mikoto (大山祇命), father of Kono-hanasakuya-hime * Hikohohodemi no Mikoto (彦火々出見命), child of Kono-hanasakuya-hime == History == === Founding === According to shrine tradition, during Emperor Sujin's era, Prince Toyokiirihiko (豊城入彦命), while subjugating the eastern provinces, prayed for victory and peace of mind at a place known as "Muro no Yashima." He is said to have enshrined the great deity of Ōmiwa (from the capital at Isonokami in Yamato) at this site, establishing the shrine.Shrine’s official literature. === Historical Overview === The mid-Heian period text "Engishiki Jinmyōchō" lists a “Ōgami Jinja” in Tsuga District, Shimotsuke Province. One theory identifies Ōmiwa Jinja with that shrine, making it a "ronsha" (disputed match).Another candidate is Taihei-san Jinja in Hirai-chō, Tochigi City. In ancient times, provincial governors (kokushi) would visit all shrines in the province, starting with the ichinomiya. To streamline this, they established a sōja near the kokufu to collectively worship all regional deities. Ōmiwa Jinja is believed to have served as the sōja of Shimotsuke Province. About 2.8 km south, the ruins of the Shimotsuke Kokuchō (provincial government offices) have been excavated. During the rebellion of Taira no Masakado (Heian period), the shrine suffered damage. Fujiwara no Hidesato and others helped rebuild it, and until the Muromachi period, it had grand buildings. However, during the Sengoku period, the remnants of Minagawa Hiroteru’s forces barricaded themselves in the shrine. Hōjō Ujinao’s army set it on fire, resulting in destruction and decline. It was said that through contributions by Tokugawa Iemitsu, who donated 30 koku of land and 10,000 pine saplings, the shrine was rebuilt in 1682 (Tenna 2) to its current form. However, no historical documents prior to the Meiji era have been found that clearly refer to this shrine as “Ōmiwa (Ōmiwa)” or “Ōmiwa.” One theory suggests that a deity from Ōmiwa Jinja (Ōmiwa Jinja in Yamato) was worshiped at another location and later merged at the Sōja of Shimotsuke.On-site information board. After the Meiji Restoration, in Meiji 6 (1873), the shrine was ranked as a Gōsha (village shrine) under the modern shrine ranking system. In Meiji 40 (1907), it was designated a shrine entitled to government offerings (Shinsen Heihaku Ryō Kyōshin Jinja), and in Meiji 44 (1911), it was promoted to Prefectural Shrine. Major renovations took place in 1924 (Taishō 13) and 1993 (Heisei 5). The Kuniho family traditionally served as hereditary Ōmiya-gūji (chief priests). === Shinhonors (Shinkai)=== * On August 29, Genkei 4 (880), it was elevated from Junior Fifth Rank, Lower Grade to Senior Fifth Rank, Upper Grade in the "Nihon Sandai Jitsuroku." The recorded deity name is "Miwa no Kami (三和神)"—some believe this refers to this shrine."Tochigi-ken no Chimei" (Heibonsha) entry on Ōmiwa Jinja. == Precincts == === Shrine Buildings === File:Oomiwa-jinja (tochigishi) honden.JPG|Honden File:Oomiwa-jinja (tochigishi) haiden.JPG|Haiden File:Oomiwa-jinja (tochigishi) kaguraden.JPG|Kagura-den === Sanctuary Forest === The forested area around Ōmiwa Jinja is designated as the Sōja Greenery Conservation Area by Tochigi Prefecture.{{Cite web |url=https://www.pref.tochigi.lg.jp/d04/30jikannti/12souja.html|title=12 Sōja Greenery Environmental Conservation Area|website=Tochigi Prefecture|accessdate=2024-11-11}} === Muro no Yashima === [[File:Oomiwa-jinja (tochigishi) muronoyashima.JPG|thumb|200px|Muro no Yashima]] [[File:TochigiOhmiwaShine2.JPG|thumb|200px|Bashō’s haiku monument before Muro no Yashima]] "Muro no Yashima" has long been known as a utamakura (poetic place name) in classical Japanese poetry. The island in the shrine’s pond is said to be its location (though some argue this is a later association).See Kōjien, "Muro no Yashima." (Kotobank [https://kotobank.jp/word/%E5%AE%A4%E3%81%AE%E5%85%AB%E5%B3%B6-642624 article]) It has been mentioned since the Nara period and appears in anthologies like the "Man’yōshū" and "Kokin Wakashū." Famous poems: * Fujiwara no Sanekata (Shika Wakashū) * Minamoto no Shigeyuki’s daughter (Zoku Goshūi Wakashū) * Ōe no Masafusa (Shinshūi Wakashū) * Fujiwara no Shunzei (Chōshū Eiso) * Fujiwara no Teika (Shin Chokusen Wakashū) Meanings associated with Muro no Yashima: * A site of a myth where Konohanasakuya-hime proved her chastity by setting herself aflame inside a room. * Possibly relates to a hearth’s smoke, turning into metaphorical love’s burning flame. * The marshy Omoigawa River basin producing water vapor or rising mist. * Over time associated with passionate love, smoke, and even kagerō (heat haze or spider’s thread). Matsuo Bashō and his companion Sora mention Muro no Yashima in "Oku no Hosomichi," but they did not include a haiku in the main text. However, in Sora’s “Haikai Kakinotame,” one of Bashō’s verses “ito asobi ni musubitsukitaru keburi kana” ("Oh, the smoke that has tied itself to the thread playing in the air!") is recorded. This haiku is inscribed on a monument erected in 1869 (Meiji 2) by the late Edo period haijin Kōun Kaku Shunpō, with calligraphy by Hagiwara Shūgan, an Edo-period calligrapher.{{Cite web |title=Tochigi Inishie no Kairō: History of Cultural Properties |url=https://www.inishie.tochigi.jp/detail.html?course_id=5&id=0|accessdate=2024-02-22}} Today’s Muro no Yashima is about 800 tsubo (approx. 2,640 square meters) of landscaped garden featuring eight small islands with small shrines dedicated to various prominent deities, including Tsukuba, Tenman, Kashima, Raiden, Sengen, Kumano, Futarayama, and Katori. There is no visible water vapor or spring water. == Subordinate Shrines == [[File:Oomiwa-jinja (tochigishi) jingu.JPG|thumb|200px|Jingū: houses the aidadono (shared) deities of the main shrine]] There are 15 shrine buildings in total: {{div col}} * Jingū * Gokoku Jinja * Fukujin Jinja * Ōsugi Jinja * Soreisha * Samon Jinja * Umon Jinja {{div col end}} '''Muro no Yashima''' {{div col}} * Sengen Jinja * Futarayama Jinja * Tsukuba Jinja * Raiden Jinja * Katori Jinja * Kashima Jinja * Kumano Jinja * Tenman-gū {{div col end}} == Annual Festivals == * Gantan-sai (January 1st) * New Year’s Pilgrimage and Shinshun Kigan-sai (January) * Setsubun-sai and Tsuina-shiki (February 3rd) * Kinen-sai (February 25th) * Chinka-sai (Early March) * Spring Grand Festival (April 16th) - Includes yabusame (horseback archery) * Hatsu-uma-sai (on the first Uma day in May) * Ōharae (June 30th) * Yashima-sai (August 1st) * Ōsugi-sai, Kaze-matsuri (Mid-August) * Shichi-go-san visits (November 15th) * Autumn Grand Festival (Mikoshi Festival) (around November 18-24) == Cultural Properties == === Tochigi City Designated Intangible Folk Cultural Properties === * Kagura of Ōmiwa Jinja - designated May 19, 1964 * Hoko (Spear) Festival of Ōmiwa Jinja - designated May 19, 1964 === Historic Sites === * Tochigi City Designated Historic Site "Shimotsuke Sōja (Muro no Yashima)" - designated February 16, 1968 == Location == * Address: Sōja-chō 477, Tochigi City, Tochigi Prefecture == Access == * About 15 minutes’ walk from Yashū-Ōtsuka Station on the Tōbu Utsunomiya Line == Surrounding Area == * Shimotsuke Kokuchō Ruins approx. 2.8 km south == Notes == {{Note help}} {{reflist}} == References == * Shrine’s official pamphlet "Ōmiwa Jinja Gaiyō" * "Nihon Rekishi Chimei Taikei: Tochigi-ken no Chimei" (Heibonsha), entry for Ōmiwa Jinja == See Also == * [[Ōmiwa Jinja (Nara)]] (Sakurai City, Nara Prefecture) == External Links == * [http://www.kuranomachi.jp/spot/soja/omiwa/ Ōmiwa Jinja] (Tochigi City Tourism Association) * [http://kir579053.kir.jp/jinjyacyo/?p=538 Ōmiwa Jinja] (Tochigi Prefecture Jinja-chō) {{Shinto Navbox}} {{DEFAULTSORT:Oomiwa Jinja Tochigishi}} [[Category:Shinto shrines in Tochigi Prefecture]] [[Category:History of Tochigi City]] [[Category:Buildings and structures in Tochigi City]] [[Category:Shikinaisha in Shimotsuke Province]] [[Category:Sōja]] [[Category:Former Prefectural shrines]] [[Category:Miwa shrines]] [[Category:Shimotsuke Province|Shrine0]] ==See Also== * [[Ichinomiya]] * [[Shimotsuke Province]] [[Ichinomiya]] ** [[Futarasan jinja]] ** [[Utsunomiya Futarayama Jinja]] ==References== {{reflist}} {{draft categories| [[Category:Sōja shrines]] [[Category:Ken-sha]] [[en:Ōmiwa Jinja (Shimotsuke)]][[Category:Shikinai Shosha]] [[Category:Miwa shrines]] [[Category:Dd]][[ja:大神神社 (栃木市)]] }} {{shinto shrines}} {{⚠️🚨COPIED from EverybodyWiki ❗❕⚠️😡😤Please respect Licence CC-BY-SA ❗}} {{Source Wikipedia}} {{Miwa and Yamato Faith}}

{{Distinguish|Omiwa Shrine}}{{draft}} {{Infobox religious building | religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]] | image = Oomiwa-jinja (tochigishi) torii.JPG | deity = all the deities of its province | type = [[Sōja (Shinto)|Sōja shrine]] }} {{ill|Ōmiwa Jinja (Shimotsuke)|lt=Ōmiwa Jinja|ja|大神神社 (栃木市)}} is a [[Sōja (Shinto)|Sōja shrine]]. It enshrines all the [[kami]] of the shrines in [[Shimotsuke Province]] Ichinomiya and Soja are not the same thing but were sometimes combinedhttps://archive.ph/wip/XtZfZ {{nihongo|'''Sōja'''|総社|}} is a type of [[Shinto shrine]] where the ''[[kami]]'' of a region are grouped together into a single sanctuary. This "region" may refer to a ''[[shōen]]'', village or geographic area, but is more generally referred to a whole [[Provinces of Japan|province]]. The term is also occasionally called "'''sōsha'''". The ''sōja'' are usually located near the [[kokufu|provincial capital]] established in the [[Nara period]] under then ''[[ritsuryō]]'' system, and can either be a newly created shrine, or a designation for an existing shrine. The "sōja" can also be the "[[ichinomiya]]" of the province, which themselves are of great ritual importance.{{cite book |last1=Herbert |first1=Jean |title=Shinto:At the Fountain-head of Japan |date=2011 |publisher=Routledge |isbn=978-0-415-59348-9 |page=105}} Whenever a new [[Kokushi (official)|kokushi]] was appointed by the central government to govern a province, it was necessary for him to visit all of the sanctuaries of his province in order to complete the rites necessary for ceremonial inauguration. Grouping the ''kami'' into one location near the capital of the province greatly facilitated this duty,{{cite book |last1=Bocking |first1=Brian |title=A Popular Dictionary of Shinto |date=2016 |publisher=Routledge |isbn=978-1138979079}} The first mention of "sōja" appeared in the [[Heian period]], in the diary of Taira no Tokinori, dated March 9, 1099 in reference to the province of [[Inaba]]. {{cite book |last1=Hardacre |first1=Helen |title=Shinto: A History |date=2016 |publisher=Oxford University Press |isbn=978-0190621711}} The name "Sōja" is also found in place names such as the city of [[Sōja, Okayama| Sōja]] in [[Okayama Prefecture]]. ==Japanese content== {{Infobox Shinto shrine | name = Ōmiwa Jinja (Oomiwa Shrine) | image = [[File:Oomiwa-jinja (tochigishi) torii.JPG|280px]]
Torii | caption = | map_type = Japan Tochigi | coordinates = {{Coord|36|24|21.30|N|139|46|55.76|E|region:JP-09_type:landmark|display=inline,title|name=Ōmiwa Jinja}} | location = Sōja-chō 477, {{ill|Tochigi (city)|ja|栃木市|lt=Tochigi City}}, {{ill|Tochigi Prefecture|ja|栃木県|lt=Tochigi Prefecture}} | deity = Yamato-Ōmononushi-Kushi-mikatama no Mikoto | type = Shikinaisha (small), a disputed identification (ronsha), Sōja of Shimotsuke Province, Former Prefectural Shrine | founded = (Trad.) 48th year of Emperor Sujin’s reign | festival = November 18–26 }} '''Ōmiwa Jinja''' (大神神社, also romanized as Oomiwa Jinja) is a {{ill|Shinto shrine|ja|神社}} located in Sōja-chō, {{ill|Tochigi (city)|ja|栃木市|lt=Tochigi City}}, {{ill|Tochigi Prefecture|ja|栃木県|lt=Tochigi Prefecture}}, Japan. It is a possible match (ronsha) for a "Shikinaisha" (small) recorded in historical texts, and is known as the Sōja (total shrine) of Shimotsuke Province. Under the modern shrine rank system of the Meiji era, it was classified as a Prefectural Shrine. Historically, it was also known by other names such as "Shimotsuke Sōja Daimyōjin," "Sōja Rokusho Daimyōjin," and "Muroyashima Sōja Daimyōjin." During the Ritsuryō era, the provincial capital (kokufu) was located about 2 km south of the shrine. Ōmiwa Jinja served as the sōja of that kokufu, and the local place name “Sōja” is derived from this shrine.{{Cite web |url=https://www.city.tochigi.lg.jp/uploaded/attachment/55689.pdf|title=Chapter 2: Historical Scenery of Tochigi City to be Maintained and Improved |website=Tochigi City|accessdate=2024-11-11|page=177}} The shrine is also known for the "Muro no Yashima" (Muro no Yashima) mentioned in Matsuo Bashō’s famous travelogue, the "Oku no Hosomichi." == Deities Enshrined == '''Principal Deity:''' * *Yamato-Ōmononushi-Kushi-mikatama no Mikoto* (倭大物主櫛𤭖玉命)According to the shrine's official literature. : In the "Izumo no Kuni no Miyatsuko Kamuyogoto," this refers to Ōmononushi no Kami. The deity is said to be an offshoot of the Ōmiwa Jinja (大神神社) in Sakurai City, Nara Prefecture. During Emperor Sujin’s reign, suffering from natural disasters and plagues, the emperor had a dream in which the deity Ōmononushi appeared and gave instructions. Following them, a man named Ootataneko performed rites at Mount Miwa, resulting in the cessation of calamities and epidemics. This story is recorded in the "Nihon Shoki." '''Additional Deities (Aiadono-matsuri):''' * Kono-hanasakuya-hime (木花咲耶姫命) * Ninigi no Mikoto (瓊々杵命), husband of Kono-hanasakuya-hime * Ōyamatsumi no Mikoto (大山祇命), father of Kono-hanasakuya-hime * Hikohohodemi no Mikoto (彦火々出見命), child of Kono-hanasakuya-hime == History == === Founding === According to shrine tradition, during Emperor Sujin's era, Prince Toyokiirihiko (豊城入彦命), while subjugating the eastern provinces, prayed for victory and peace of mind at a place known as "Muro no Yashima." He is said to have enshrined the great deity of Ōmiwa (from the capital at Isonokami in Yamato) at this site, establishing the shrine.Shrine’s official literature. === Historical Overview === The mid-Heian period text "Engishiki Jinmyōchō" lists a “Ōgami Jinja” in Tsuga District, Shimotsuke Province. One theory identifies Ōmiwa Jinja with that shrine, making it a "ronsha" (disputed match).Another candidate is Taihei-san Jinja in Hirai-chō, Tochigi City. In ancient times, provincial governors (kokushi) would visit all shrines in the province, starting with the ichinomiya. To streamline this, they established a sōja near the kokufu to collectively worship all regional deities. Ōmiwa Jinja is believed to have served as the sōja of Shimotsuke Province. About 2.8 km south, the ruins of the Shimotsuke Kokuchō (provincial government offices) have been excavated. During the rebellion of Taira no Masakado (Heian period), the shrine suffered damage. Fujiwara no Hidesato and others helped rebuild it, and until the Muromachi period, it had grand buildings. However, during the Sengoku period, the remnants of Minagawa Hiroteru’s forces barricaded themselves in the shrine. Hōjō Ujinao’s army set it on fire, resulting in destruction and decline. It was said that through contributions by Tokugawa Iemitsu, who donated 30 koku of land and 10,000 pine saplings, the shrine was rebuilt in 1682 (Tenna 2) to its current form. However, no historical documents prior to the Meiji era have been found that clearly refer to this shrine as “Ōmiwa (Ōmiwa)” or “Ōmiwa.” One theory suggests that a deity from Ōmiwa Jinja (Ōmiwa Jinja in Yamato) was worshiped at another location and later merged at the Sōja of Shimotsuke.On-site information board. After the Meiji Restoration, in Meiji 6 (1873), the shrine was ranked as a Gōsha (village shrine) under the modern shrine ranking system. In Meiji 40 (1907), it was designated a shrine entitled to government offerings (Shinsen Heihaku Ryō Kyōshin Jinja), and in Meiji 44 (1911), it was promoted to Prefectural Shrine. Major renovations took place in 1924 (Taishō 13) and 1993 (Heisei 5). The Kuniho family traditionally served as hereditary Ōmiya-gūji (chief priests). === Shinhonors (Shinkai)=== * On August 29, Genkei 4 (880), it was elevated from Junior Fifth Rank, Lower Grade to Senior Fifth Rank, Upper Grade in the "Nihon Sandai Jitsuroku." The recorded deity name is "Miwa no Kami (三和神)"—some believe this refers to this shrine."Tochigi-ken no Chimei" (Heibonsha) entry on Ōmiwa Jinja. == Precincts == === Shrine Buildings === File:Oomiwa-jinja (tochigishi) honden.JPG|Honden File:Oomiwa-jinja (tochigishi) haiden.JPG|Haiden File:Oomiwa-jinja (tochigishi) kaguraden.JPG|Kagura-den === Sanctuary Forest === The forested area around Ōmiwa Jinja is designated as the Sōja Greenery Conservation Area by Tochigi Prefecture.{{Cite web |url=https://www.pref.tochigi.lg.jp/d04/30jikannti/12souja.html|title=12 Sōja Greenery Environmental Conservation Area|website=Tochigi Prefecture|accessdate=2024-11-11}} === Muro no Yashima === [[File:Oomiwa-jinja (tochigishi) muronoyashima.JPG|thumb|200px|Muro no Yashima]] [[File:TochigiOhmiwaShine2.JPG|thumb|200px|Bashō’s haiku monument before Muro no Yashima]] "Muro no Yashima" has long been known as a utamakura (poetic place name) in classical Japanese poetry. The island in the shrine’s pond is said to be its location (though some argue this is a later association).See Kōjien, "Muro no Yashima." (Kotobank [https://kotobank.jp/word/%E5%AE%A4%E3%81%AE%E5%85%AB%E5%B3%B6-642624 article]) It has been mentioned since the Nara period and appears in anthologies like the "Man’yōshū" and "Kokin Wakashū." Famous poems: * Fujiwara no Sanekata (Shika Wakashū) * Minamoto no Shigeyuki’s daughter (Zoku Goshūi Wakashū) * Ōe no Masafusa (Shinshūi Wakashū) * Fujiwara no Shunzei (Chōshū Eiso) * Fujiwara no Teika (Shin Chokusen Wakashū) Meanings associated with Muro no Yashima: * A site of a myth where Konohanasakuya-hime proved her chastity by setting herself aflame inside a room. * Possibly relates to a hearth’s smoke, turning into metaphorical love’s burning flame. * The marshy Omoigawa River basin producing water vapor or rising mist. * Over time associated with passionate love, smoke, and even kagerō (heat haze or spider’s thread). Matsuo Bashō and his companion Sora mention Muro no Yashima in "Oku no Hosomichi," but they did not include a haiku in the main text. However, in Sora’s “Haikai Kakinotame,” one of Bashō’s verses “ito asobi ni musubitsukitaru keburi kana” ("Oh, the smoke that has tied itself to the thread playing in the air!") is recorded. This haiku is inscribed on a monument erected in 1869 (Meiji 2) by the late Edo period haijin Kōun Kaku Shunpō, with calligraphy by Hagiwara Shūgan, an Edo-period calligrapher.{{Cite web |title=Tochigi Inishie no Kairō: History of Cultural Properties |url=https://www.inishie.tochigi.jp/detail.html?course_id=5&id=0|accessdate=2024-02-22}} Today’s Muro no Yashima is about 800 tsubo (approx. 2,640 square meters) of landscaped garden featuring eight small islands with small shrines dedicated to various prominent deities, including Tsukuba, Tenman, Kashima, Raiden, Sengen, Kumano, Futarayama, and Katori. There is no visible water vapor or spring water. == Subordinate Shrines == [[File:Oomiwa-jinja (tochigishi) jingu.JPG|thumb|200px|Jingū: houses the aidadono (shared) deities of the main shrine]] There are 15 shrine buildings in total: {{div col}} * Jingū * Gokoku Jinja * Fukujin Jinja * Ōsugi Jinja * Soreisha * Samon Jinja * Umon Jinja {{div col end}} '''Muro no Yashima''' {{div col}} * Sengen Jinja * Futarayama Jinja * Tsukuba Jinja * Raiden Jinja * Katori Jinja * Kashima Jinja * Kumano Jinja * Tenman-gū {{div col end}} == Annual Festivals == * Gantan-sai (January 1st) * New Year’s Pilgrimage and Shinshun Kigan-sai (January) * Setsubun-sai and Tsuina-shiki (February 3rd) * Kinen-sai (February 25th) * Chinka-sai (Early March) * Spring Grand Festival (April 16th) - Includes yabusame (horseback archery) * Hatsu-uma-sai (on the first Uma day in May) * Ōharae (June 30th) * Yashima-sai (August 1st) * Ōsugi-sai, Kaze-matsuri (Mid-August) * Shichi-go-san visits (November 15th) * Autumn Grand Festival (Mikoshi Festival) (around November 18-24) == Cultural Properties == === Tochigi City Designated Intangible Folk Cultural Properties === * Kagura of Ōmiwa Jinja - designated May 19, 1964 * Hoko (Spear) Festival of Ōmiwa Jinja - designated May 19, 1964 === Historic Sites === * Tochigi City Designated Historic Site "Shimotsuke Sōja (Muro no Yashima)" - designated February 16, 1968 == Location == * Address: Sōja-chō 477, Tochigi City, Tochigi Prefecture == Access == * About 15 minutes’ walk from Yashū-Ōtsuka Station on the Tōbu Utsunomiya Line == Surrounding Area == * Shimotsuke Kokuchō Ruins approx. 2.8 km south == Notes == {{Note help}} {{reflist}} == References == * Shrine’s official pamphlet "Ōmiwa Jinja Gaiyō" * "Nihon Rekishi Chimei Taikei: Tochigi-ken no Chimei" (Heibonsha), entry for Ōmiwa Jinja == See Also == * [[Ōmiwa Jinja (Nara)]] (Sakurai City, Nara Prefecture) == External Links == * [http://www.kuranomachi.jp/spot/soja/omiwa/ Ōmiwa Jinja] (Tochigi City Tourism Association) * [http://kir579053.kir.jp/jinjyacyo/?p=538 Ōmiwa Jinja] (Tochigi Prefecture Jinja-chō) {{Shinto Navbox}} {{DEFAULTSORT:Oomiwa Jinja Tochigishi}} [[Category:Shinto shrines in Tochigi Prefecture]] [[Category:History of Tochigi City]] [[Category:Buildings and structures in Tochigi City]] [[Category:Shikinaisha in Shimotsuke Province]] [[Category:Sōja]] [[Category:Former Prefectural shrines]] [[Category:Miwa shrines]] [[Category:Shimotsuke Province|Shrine0]] ==See Also== * [[Ichinomiya]] * [[Shimotsuke Province]] [[Ichinomiya]] ** [[Futarasan jinja]] ** [[Utsunomiya Futarayama Jinja]] ==References== {{reflist}} {{draft categories| [[Category:Sōja shrines]] [[Category:Ken-sha]] [[en:Ōmiwa Jinja (Shimotsuke)]][[Category:Shikinai Shosha]] [[Category:Miwa shrines]] [[Category:pages from wikipedia]] [[ja:大神神社 (栃木市)]] }} {{shinto shrines}} {{⚠️🚨COPIED from EverybodyWiki ❗❕⚠️😡😤Please respect Licence CC-BY-SA ❗}} {{Source Wikipedia}} {{Miwa and Yamato Faith}}

Ōmiwa Jinja served as the sōja of that kokufu, and the local place name “Sōja” is derived from this shrine.{{Cite web |url=https://www.city.tochigi.lg.jp/uploaded/attachment/55689.pdf|title=Chapter 2: Historical Scenery of Tochigi City to be Maintained and Improved |website=Tochigi City|accessdate=2024-11-11|page=177}} The shrine is also known for the "Muro no Yashima" (Muro no Yashima) mentioned in Matsuo Bashō’s famous travelogue, the "Oku no Hosomichi." == Deities Enshrined == '''Principal Deity:''' * *Yamato-Ōmononushi-Kushi-mikatama no Mikoto* (倭大物主櫛𤭖玉命)According to the shrine's official literature. : In the "Izumo no Kuni no Miyatsuko Kamuyogoto," this refers to Ōmononushi no Kami. The deity is said to be an offshoot of the Ōmiwa Jinja (大神神社) in Sakurai City, Nara Prefecture. During Emperor Sujin’s reign, suffering from natural disasters and plagues, the emperor had a dream in which the deity Ōmononushi appeared and gave instructions. Following them, a man named Ootataneko performed rites at Mount Miwa, resulting in the cessation of calamities and epidemics. This story is recorded in the "Nihon Shoki." '''Additional Deities (Aiadono-matsuri):''' * Kono-hanasakuya-hime (木花咲耶姫命) * Ninigi no Mikoto (瓊々杵命), husband of Kono-hanasakuya-hime * Ōyamatsumi no Mikoto (大山祇命), father of Kono-hanasakuya-hime * Hikohohodemi no Mikoto (彦火々出見命), child of Kono-hanasakuya-hime == History == === Founding === According to shrine tradition, during Emperor Sujin's era, Prince Toyokiirihiko (豊城入彦命), while subjugating the eastern provinces, prayed for victory and peace of mind at a place known as "Muro no Yashima." He is said to have enshrined the great deity of Ōmiwa (from the capital at Isonokami in Yamato) at this site, establishing the shrine.Shrine’s official literature. === Historical Overview === The mid-Heian period text "Engishiki Jinmyōchō" lists a “Ōgami Jinja” in Tsuga District, Shimotsuke Province. One theory identifies Ōmiwa Jinja with that shrine, making it a "ronsha" (disputed match).Another candidate is Taihei-san Jinja in Hirai-chō, Tochigi City. In ancient times, provincial governors (kokushi) would visit all shrines in the province, starting with the ichinomiya. To streamline this, they established a sōja near the kokufu to collectively worship all regional deities. Ōmiwa Jinja is believed to have served as the sōja of Shimotsuke Province. About 2.8 km south, the ruins of the Shimotsuke Kokuchō (provincial government offices) have been excavated. During the rebellion of Taira no Masakado (Heian period), the shrine suffered damage. Fujiwara no Hidesato and others helped rebuild it, and until the Muromachi period, it had grand buildings. However, during the Sengoku period, the remnants of Minagawa Hiroteru’s forces barricaded themselves in the shrine. Hōjō Ujinao’s army set it on fire, resulting in destruction and decline. It was said that through contributions by Tokugawa Iemitsu, who donated 30 koku of land and 10,000 pine saplings, the shrine was rebuilt in 1682 (Tenna 2) to its current form. However, no historical documents prior to the Meiji era have been found that clearly refer to this shrine as “Ōmiwa (Ōmiwa)” or “Ōmiwa.” One theory suggests that a deity from Ōmiwa Jinja (Ōmiwa Jinja in Yamato) was worshiped at another location and later merged at the Sōja of Shimotsuke.On-site information board. After the Meiji Restoration, in Meiji 6 (1873), the shrine was ranked as a Gōsha (village shrine) under the modern shrine ranking system. In Meiji 40 (1907), it was designated a shrine entitled to government offerings (Shinsen Heihaku Ryō Kyōshin Jinja), and in Meiji 44 (1911), it was promoted to Prefectural Shrine. Major renovations took place in 1924 (Taishō 13) and 1993 (Heisei 5). The Kuniho family traditionally served as hereditary Ōmiya-gūji (chief priests). === Shinhonors (Shinkai)=== * On August 29, Genkei 4 (880), it was elevated from Junior Fifth Rank, Lower Grade to Senior Fifth Rank, Upper Grade in the "Nihon Sandai Jitsuroku." The recorded deity name is "Miwa no Kami (三和神)"—some believe this refers to this shrine."Tochigi-ken no Chimei" (Heibonsha) entry on Ōmiwa Jinja. == Precincts == === Shrine Buildings === File:Oomiwa-jinja (tochigishi) honden.JPG|Honden File:Oomiwa-jinja (tochigishi) haiden.JPG|Haiden File:Oomiwa-jinja (tochigishi) kaguraden.JPG|Kagura-den === Sanctuary Forest === The forested area around Ōmiwa Jinja is designated as the Sōja Greenery Conservation Area by Tochigi Prefecture.{{Cite web |url=https://www.pref.tochigi.lg.jp/d04/30jikannti/12souja.html|title=12 Sōja Greenery Environmental Conservation Area|website=Tochigi Prefecture|accessdate=2024-11-11}} === Muro no Yashima === [[File:Oomiwa-jinja (tochigishi) muronoyashima.JPG|thumb|200px|Muro no Yashima]] [[File:TochigiOhmiwaShine2.JPG|thumb|200px|Bashō’s haiku monument before Muro no Yashima]] "Muro no Yashima" has long been known as a utamakura (poetic place name) in classical Japanese poetry. The island in the shrine’s pond is said to be its location (though some argue this is a later association).See Kōjien, "Muro no Yashima." (Kotobank [https://kotobank.jp/word/%E5%AE%A4%E3%81%AE%E5%85%AB%E5%B3%B6-642624 article]) It has been mentioned since the Nara period and appears in anthologies like the "Man’yōshū" and "Kokin Wakashū." Famous poems: * Fujiwara no Sanekata (Shika Wakashū) * Minamoto no Shigeyuki’s daughter (Zoku Goshūi Wakashū) * Ōe no Masafusa (Shinshūi Wakashū) * Fujiwara no Shunzei (Chōshū Eiso) * Fujiwara no Teika (Shin Chokusen Wakashū) Meanings associated with Muro no Yashima: * A site of a myth where Konohanasakuya-hime proved her chastity by setting herself aflame inside a room. * Possibly relates to a hearth’s smoke, turning into metaphorical love’s burning flame. * The marshy Omoigawa River basin producing water vapor or rising mist. * Over time associated with passionate love, smoke, and even kagerō (heat haze or spider’s thread). Matsuo Bashō and his companion Sora mention Muro no Yashima in "Oku no Hosomichi," but they did not include a haiku in the main text. However, in Sora’s “Haikai Kakinotame,” one of Bashō’s verses “ito asobi ni musubitsukitaru keburi kana” ("Oh, the smoke that has tied itself to the thread playing in the air!") is recorded. This haiku is inscribed on a monument erected in 1869 (Meiji 2) by the late Edo period haijin Kōun Kaku Shunpō, with calligraphy by Hagiwara Shūgan, an Edo-period calligrapher.{{Cite web |title=Tochigi Inishie no Kairō: History of Cultural Properties |url=https://www.inishie.tochigi.jp/detail.html?course_id=5&id=0|accessdate=2024-02-22}} Today’s Muro no Yashima is about 800 tsubo (approx. 2,640 square meters) of landscaped garden featuring eight small islands with small shrines dedicated to various prominent deities, including Tsukuba, Tenman, Kashima, Raiden, Sengen, Kumano, Futarayama, and Katori. There is no visible water vapor or spring water. == Subordinate Shrines == [[File:Oomiwa-jinja (tochigishi) jingu.JPG|thumb|200px|Jingū: houses the aidadono (shared) deities of the main shrine]] There are 15 shrine buildings in total: {{div col}} * Jingū * Gokoku Jinja * Fukujin Jinja * Ōsugi Jinja * Soreisha * Samon Jinja * Umon Jinja {{div col end}} '''Muro no Yashima''' {{div col}} * Sengen Jinja * Futarayama Jinja * Tsukuba Jinja * Raiden Jinja * Katori Jinja * Kashima Jinja * Kumano Jinja * Tenman-gū {{div col end}} == Annual Festivals == * Gantan-sai (January 1st) * New Year’s Pilgrimage and Shinshun Kigan-sai (January) * Setsubun-sai and Tsuina-shiki (February 3rd) * Kinen-sai (February 25th) * Chinka-sai (Early March) * Spring Grand Festival (April 16th) - Includes yabusame (horseback archery) * Hatsu-uma-sai (on the first Uma day in May) * Ōharae (June 30th) * Yashima-sai (August 1st) * Ōsugi-sai, Kaze-matsuri (Mid-August) * Shichi-go-san visits (November 15th) * Autumn Grand Festival (Mikoshi Festival) (around November 18-24) == Cultural Properties == === Tochigi City Designated Intangible Folk Cultural Properties === * Kagura of Ōmiwa Jinja - designated May 19, 1964 * Hoko (Spear) Festival of Ōmiwa Jinja - designated May 19, 1964 === Historic Sites === * Tochigi City Designated Historic Site "Shimotsuke Sōja (Muro no Yashima)" - designated February 16, 1968 == Location == * Address: Sōja-chō 477, Tochigi City, Tochigi Prefecture == Access == * About 15 minutes’ walk from Yashū-Ōtsuka Station on the Tōbu Utsunomiya Line == Surrounding Area == * Shimotsuke Kokuchō Ruins approx. 2.8 km south == Notes == {{Note help}} {{reflist}} == References == * Shrine’s official pamphlet "Ōmiwa Jinja Gaiyō" * "Nihon Rekishi Chimei Taikei: Tochigi-ken no Chimei" (Heibonsha), entry for Ōmiwa Jinja == See Also == * [[Ōmiwa Jinja (Nara)]] (Sakurai City, Nara Prefecture) == External Links == * [http://www.kuranomachi.jp/spot/soja/omiwa/ Ōmiwa Jinja] (Tochigi City Tourism Association) * [http://kir579053.kir.jp/jinjyacyo/?p=538 Ōmiwa Jinja] (Tochigi Prefecture Jinja-chō) {{Shinto Navbox}} {{DEFAULTSORT:Oomiwa Jinja Tochigishi}} [[Category:Shinto shrines in Tochigi Prefecture]] [[Category:History of Tochigi City]] [[Category:Buildings and structures in Tochigi City]] [[Category:Shikinaisha in Shimotsuke Province]] [[Category:Sōja]] [[Category:Former Prefectural shrines]] [[Category:Miwa shrines]] [[Category:Shimotsuke Province|Shrine0]] ==See Also== * [[Ichinomiya]] * [[Shimotsuke Province]] [[Ichinomiya]] ** [[Futarasan jinja]] ** [[Utsunomiya Futarayama Jinja]] ==References== {{reflist}} {{draft categories| [[Category:Sōja shrines]] [[Category:Ken-sha]] [[en:Ōmiwa Jinja (Shimotsuke)]][[Category:Shikinai Shosha]] [[Category:Miwa shrines]] [[ja:大神神社 (栃木市)]] }} {{shinto shrines}} {{⚠️🚨COPIED from EverybodyWiki ❗❕⚠️😡😤Please respect Licence CC-BY-SA ❗}} {{Source Wikipedia}} {{Miwa and Yamato Faith}}

It enshrines all the [[kami]] of the shrines in [[Shimotsuke Province]] Ichinomiya and Soja are not the same thing but were sometimes combinedhttps://archive.ph/wip/XtZfZ {{nihongo|'''Sōja'''|総社|}} is a type of [[Shinto shrine]] where the ''[[kami]]'' of a region are grouped together into a single sanctuary. This "region" may refer to a ''[[shōen]]'', village or geographic area, but is more generally referred to a whole [[Provinces of Japan|province]]. The term is also occasionally called "'''sōsha'''". The ''sōja'' are usually located near the [[kokufu|provincial capital]] established in the [[Nara period]] under then ''[[ritsuryō]]'' system, and can either be a newly created shrine, or a designation for an existing shrine. The "sōja" can also be the "[[ichinomiya]]" of the province, which themselves are of great ritual importance.{{cite book |last1=Herbert |first1=Jean |title=Shinto:At the Fountain-head of Japan |date=2011 |publisher=Routledge |isbn=978-0-415-59348-9 |page=105}} Whenever a new [[Kokushi (official)|kokushi]] was appointed by the central government to govern a province, it was necessary for him to visit all of the sanctuaries of his province in order to complete the rites necessary for ceremonial inauguration. Grouping the ''kami'' into one location near the capital of the province greatly facilitated this duty,{{cite book |last1=Bocking |first1=Brian |title=A Popular Dictionary of Shinto |date=2016 |publisher=Routledge |isbn=978-1138979079}} The first mention of "sōja" appeared in the [[Heian period]], in the diary of Taira no Tokinori, dated March 9, 1099 in reference to the province of [[Inaba]]. {{cite book |last1=Hardacre |first1=Helen |title=Shinto: A History |date=2016 |publisher=Oxford University Press |isbn=978-0190621711}} The name "Sōja" is also found in place names such as the city of [[Sōja, Okayama| Sōja]] in [[Okayama Prefecture]]. ==Japanese content== {{Infobox Shinto shrine | name = Ōmiwa Jinja (Oomiwa Shrine) | image = [[File:Oomiwa-jinja (tochigishi) torii.JPG|280px]]

It is a possible match (ronsha) for a "Shikinaisha" (small) recorded in historical texts, and is known as the Sōja (total shrine) of Shimotsuke Province. Under the modern shrine rank system of the Meiji era, it was classified as a Prefectural Shrine. Historically, it was also known by other names such as "Shimotsuke Sōja Daimyōjin," "Sōja Rokusho Daimyōjin," and "Muroyashima Sōja Daimyōjin." During the Ritsuryō era, the provincial capital (kokufu) was located about 2 km south of the shrine. This "region" may refer to a ''[[shōen]]'', village or geographic area, but is more generally referred to a whole [[Provinces of Japan|province]]. The term is also occasionally called "'''sōsha'''". The ''sōja'' are usually located near the [[kokufu|provincial capital]] established in the [[Nara period]] under then ''[[ritsuryō]]'' system, and can either be a newly created shrine, or a designation for an existing shrine. The "sōja" can also be the "[[ichinomiya]]" of the province, which themselves are of great ritual importance.{{cite book |last1=Herbert |first1=Jean |title=Shinto:At the Fountain-head of Japan |date=2011 |publisher=Routledge |isbn=978-0-415-59348-9 |page=105}} Whenever a new [[Kokushi (official)|kokushi]] was appointed by the central government to govern a province, it was necessary for him to visit all of the sanctuaries of his province in order to complete the rites necessary for ceremonial inauguration. Grouping the ''kami'' into one location near the capital of the province greatly facilitated this duty,{{cite book |last1=Bocking |first1=Brian |title=A Popular Dictionary of Shinto |date=2016 |publisher=Routledge |isbn=978-1138979079}} The first mention of "sōja" appeared in the [[Heian period]], in the diary of Taira no Tokinori, dated March 9, 1099 in reference to the province of [[Inaba]]. {{cite book |last1=Hardacre |first1=Helen |title=Shinto: A History |date=2016 |publisher=Oxford University Press |isbn=978-0190621711}} The name "Sōja" is also found in place names such as the city of [[Sōja, Okayama| Sōja]] in [[Okayama Prefecture]]. ==Japanese content== {{Infobox Shinto shrine | name = Ōmiwa Jinja (Oomiwa Shrine) | image = [[File:Oomiwa-jinja (tochigishi) torii.JPG|280px]]
Torii | caption = | map_type = Japan Tochigi | coordinates = {{Coord|36|24|21.30|N|139|46|55.76|E|region:JP-09_type:landmark|display=inline,title|name=Ōmiwa Jinja}} | location = Sōja-chō 477, {{ill|Tochigi (city)|ja|栃木市|lt=Tochigi City}}, {{ill|Tochigi Prefecture|ja|栃木県|lt=Tochigi Prefecture}} | deity = Yamato-Ōmononushi-Kushi-mikatama no Mikoto | type = Shikinaisha (small), a disputed identification (ronsha), Sōja of Shimotsuke Province, Former Prefectural Shrine | founded = (Trad.) 48th year of Emperor Sujin’s reign | festival = November 18–26 }} '''Ōmiwa Jinja''' (大神神社, also romanized as Oomiwa Jinja) is a {{ill|Shinto shrine|ja|神社}} located in Sōja-chō, {{ill|Tochigi (city)|ja|栃木市|lt=Tochigi City}}, {{ill|Tochigi Prefecture|ja|栃木県|lt=Tochigi Prefecture}}, Japan. It is a possible match (ronsha) for a "Shikinaisha" (small) recorded in historical texts, and is known as the Sōja (total shrine) of Shimotsuke Province. Under the modern shrine rank system of the Meiji era, it was classified as a Prefectural Shrine. Historically, it was also known by other names such as "Shimotsuke Sōja Daimyōjin," "Sōja Rokusho Daimyōjin," and "Muroyashima Sōja Daimyōjin." During the Ritsuryō era, the provincial capital (kokufu) was located about 2 km south of the shrine. Ōmiwa Jinja served as the sōja of that kokufu, and the local place name “Sōja” is derived from this shrine.{{Cite web |url=https://www.city.tochigi.lg.jp/uploaded/attachment/55689.pdf|title=Chapter 2: Historical Scenery of Tochigi City to be Maintained and Improved |website=Tochigi City|accessdate=2024-11-11|page=177}} The shrine is also known for the "Muro no Yashima" (Muro no Yashima) mentioned in Matsuo Bashō’s famous travelogue, the "Oku no Hosomichi." == Deities Enshrined == '''Principal Deity:''' * *Yamato-Ōmononushi-Kushi-mikatama no Mikoto* (倭大物主櫛𤭖玉命)According to the shrine's official literature. : In the "Izumo no Kuni no Miyatsuko Kamuyogoto," this refers to Ōmononushi no Kami. The deity is said to be an offshoot of the Ōmiwa Jinja (大神神社) in Sakurai City, Nara Prefecture. During Emperor Sujin’s reign, suffering from natural disasters and plagues, the emperor had a dream in which the deity Ōmononushi appeared and gave instructions. Following them, a man named Ootataneko performed rites at Mount Miwa, resulting in the cessation of calamities and epidemics. This story is recorded in the "Nihon Shoki." '''Additional Deities (Aiadono-matsuri):''' * Kono-hanasakuya-hime (木花咲耶姫命) * Ninigi no Mikoto (瓊々杵命), husband of Kono-hanasakuya-hime * Ōyamatsumi no Mikoto (大山祇命), father of Kono-hanasakuya-hime * Hikohohodemi no Mikoto (彦火々出見命), child of Kono-hanasakuya-hime == History == === Founding === According to shrine tradition, during Emperor Sujin's era, Prince Toyokiirihiko (豊城入彦命), while subjugating the eastern provinces, prayed for victory and peace of mind at a place known as "Muro no Yashima." He is said to have enshrined the great deity of Ōmiwa (from the capital at Isonokami in Yamato) at this site, establishing the shrine.Shrine’s official literature. === Historical Overview === The mid-Heian period text "Engishiki Jinmyōchō" lists a “Ōgami Jinja” in Tsuga District, Shimotsuke Province. One theory identifies Ōmiwa Jinja with that shrine, making it a "ronsha" (disputed match).Another candidate is Taihei-san Jinja in Hirai-chō, Tochigi City. In ancient times, provincial governors (kokushi) would visit all shrines in the province, starting with the ichinomiya. To streamline this, they established a sōja near the kokufu to collectively worship all regional deities. Ōmiwa Jinja is believed to have served as the sōja of Shimotsuke Province. About 2.8 km south, the ruins of the Shimotsuke Kokuchō (provincial government offices) have been excavated. During the rebellion of Taira no Masakado (Heian period), the shrine suffered damage. Fujiwara no Hidesato and others helped rebuild it, and until the Muromachi period, it had grand buildings. However, during the Sengoku period, the remnants of Minagawa Hiroteru’s forces barricaded themselves in the shrine. Hōjō Ujinao’s army set it on fire, resulting in destruction and decline. It was said that through contributions by Tokugawa Iemitsu, who donated 30 koku of land and 10,000 pine saplings, the shrine was rebuilt in 1682 (Tenna 2) to its current form. However, no historical documents prior to the Meiji era have been found that clearly refer to this shrine as “Ōmiwa (Ōmiwa)” or “Ōmiwa.” One theory suggests that a deity from Ōmiwa Jinja (Ōmiwa Jinja in Yamato) was worshiped at another location and later merged at the Sōja of Shimotsuke.On-site information board. After the Meiji Restoration, in Meiji 6 (1873), the shrine was ranked as a Gōsha (village shrine) under the modern shrine ranking system. In Meiji 40 (1907), it was designated a shrine entitled to government offerings (Shinsen Heihaku Ryō Kyōshin Jinja), and in Meiji 44 (1911), it was promoted to Prefectural Shrine. Major renovations took place in 1924 (Taishō 13) and 1993 (Heisei 5). The Kuniho family traditionally served as hereditary Ōmiya-gūji (chief priests). === Shinhonors (Shinkai)=== * On August 29, Genkei 4 (880), it was elevated from Junior Fifth Rank, Lower Grade to Senior Fifth Rank, Upper Grade in the "Nihon Sandai Jitsuroku." The recorded deity name is "Miwa no Kami (三和神)"—some believe this refers to this shrine."Tochigi-ken no Chimei" (Heibonsha) entry on Ōmiwa Jinja. == Precincts == === Shrine Buildings === File:Oomiwa-jinja (tochigishi) honden.JPG|Honden File:Oomiwa-jinja (tochigishi) haiden.JPG|Haiden File:Oomiwa-jinja (tochigishi) kaguraden.JPG|Kagura-den === Sanctuary Forest === The forested area around Ōmiwa Jinja is designated as the Sōja Greenery Conservation Area by Tochigi Prefecture.{{Cite web |url=https://www.pref.tochigi.lg.jp/d04/30jikannti/12souja.html|title=12 Sōja Greenery Environmental Conservation Area|website=Tochigi Prefecture|accessdate=2024-11-11}} === Muro no Yashima === [[File:Oomiwa-jinja (tochigishi) muronoyashima.JPG|thumb|200px|Muro no Yashima]] [[File:TochigiOhmiwaShine2.JPG|thumb|200px|Bashō’s haiku monument before Muro no Yashima]] "Muro no Yashima" has long been known as a utamakura (poetic place name) in classical Japanese poetry. The island in the shrine’s pond is said to be its location (though some argue this is a later association).See Kōjien, "Muro no Yashima." (Kotobank [https://kotobank.jp/word/%E5%AE%A4%E3%81%AE%E5%85%AB%E5%B3%B6-642624 article]) It has been mentioned since the Nara period and appears in anthologies like the "Man’yōshū" and "Kokin Wakashū." Famous poems: * Fujiwara no Sanekata (Shika Wakashū) * Minamoto no Shigeyuki’s daughter (Zoku Goshūi Wakashū) * Ōe no Masafusa (Shinshūi Wakashū) * Fujiwara no Shunzei (Chōshū Eiso) * Fujiwara no Teika (Shin Chokusen Wakashū) Meanings associated with Muro no Yashima: * A site of a myth where Konohanasakuya-hime proved her chastity by setting herself aflame inside a room. * Possibly relates to a hearth’s smoke, turning into metaphorical love’s burning flame. * The marshy Omoigawa River basin producing water vapor or rising mist. * Over time associated with passionate love, smoke, and even kagerō (heat haze or spider’s thread). Matsuo Bashō and his companion Sora mention Muro no Yashima in "Oku no Hosomichi," but they did not include a haiku in the main text. However, in Sora’s “Haikai Kakinotame,” one of Bashō’s verses “ito asobi ni musubitsukitaru keburi kana” ("Oh, the smoke that has tied itself to the thread playing in the air!") is recorded. This haiku is inscribed on a monument erected in 1869 (Meiji 2) by the late Edo period haijin Kōun Kaku Shunpō, with calligraphy by Hagiwara Shūgan, an Edo-period calligrapher.{{Cite web |title=Tochigi Inishie no Kairō: History of Cultural Properties |url=https://www.inishie.tochigi.jp/detail.html?course_id=5&id=0|accessdate=2024-02-22}} Today’s Muro no Yashima is about 800 tsubo (approx. 2,640 square meters) of landscaped garden featuring eight small islands with small shrines dedicated to various prominent deities, including Tsukuba, Tenman, Kashima, Raiden, Sengen, Kumano, Futarayama, and Katori. There is no visible water vapor or spring water. == Subordinate Shrines == [[File:Oomiwa-jinja (tochigishi) jingu.JPG|thumb|200px|Jingū: houses the aidadono (shared) deities of the main shrine]] There are 15 shrine buildings in total: {{div col}} * Jingū * Gokoku Jinja * Fukujin Jinja * Ōsugi Jinja * Soreisha * Samon Jinja * Umon Jinja {{div col end}} '''Muro no Yashima''' {{div col}} * Sengen Jinja * Futarayama Jinja * Tsukuba Jinja * Raiden Jinja * Katori Jinja * Kashima Jinja * Kumano Jinja * Tenman-gū {{div col end}} == Annual Festivals == * Gantan-sai (January 1st) * New Year’s Pilgrimage and Shinshun Kigan-sai (January) * Setsubun-sai and Tsuina-shiki (February 3rd) * Kinen-sai (February 25th) * Chinka-sai (Early March) * Spring Grand Festival (April 16th) - Includes yabusame (horseback archery) * Hatsu-uma-sai (on the first Uma day in May) * Ōharae (June 30th) * Yashima-sai (August 1st) * Ōsugi-sai, Kaze-matsuri (Mid-August) * Shichi-go-san visits (November 15th) * Autumn Grand Festival (Mikoshi Festival) (around November 18-24) == Cultural Properties == === Tochigi City Designated Intangible Folk Cultural Properties === * Kagura of Ōmiwa Jinja - designated May 19, 1964 * Hoko (Spear) Festival of Ōmiwa Jinja - designated May 19, 1964 === Historic Sites === * Tochigi City Designated Historic Site "Shimotsuke Sōja (Muro no Yashima)" - designated February 16, 1968 == Location == * Address: Sōja-chō 477, Tochigi City, Tochigi Prefecture == Access == * About 15 minutes’ walk from Yashū-Ōtsuka Station on the Tōbu Utsunomiya Line == Surrounding Area == * Shimotsuke Kokuchō Ruins approx. 2.8 km south == Notes == {{Note help}} {{reflist}} == References == * Shrine’s official pamphlet "Ōmiwa Jinja Gaiyō" * "Nihon Rekishi Chimei Taikei: Tochigi-ken no Chimei" (Heibonsha), entry for Ōmiwa Jinja == See Also == * [[Ōmiwa Jinja (Nara)]] (Sakurai City, Nara Prefecture) == External Links == * [http://www.kuranomachi.jp/spot/soja/omiwa/ Ōmiwa Jinja] (Tochigi City Tourism Association) * [http://kir579053.kir.jp/jinjyacyo/?p=538 Ōmiwa Jinja] (Tochigi Prefecture Jinja-chō) {{Shinto Navbox}} {{DEFAULTSORT:Oomiwa Jinja Tochigishi}} [[Category:Shinto shrines in Tochigi Prefecture]] [[Category:History of Tochigi City]] [[Category:Buildings and structures in Tochigi City]] [[Category:Shikinaisha in Shimotsuke Province]] [[Category:Former Prefectural shrines]] [[Category:Miwa shrines]] [[Category:Shimotsuke Province|Shrine0]] ==See Also== * [[Ichinomiya]] * [[Shimotsuke Province]] [[Ichinomiya]] ** [[Futarasan jinja]] ** [[Utsunomiya Futarayama Jinja]] ==References== {{reflist}} {{draft categories| [[Category:Sōja shrines]] [[Category:Ken-sha]] [[en:Ōmiwa Jinja (Shimotsuke)]][[Category:Shikinai Shosha]] [[Category:Miwa shrines]] [[Category:original pages]][[Category:original pages]] [[ja:大神神社 (栃木市)]] }} {{shinto shrines}} {{⚠️🚨COPIED from EverybodyWiki ❗❕⚠️😡😤Please respect Licence CC-BY-SA ❗}} {{Source Wikipedia}} {{Miwa and Yamato Faith}}

There is no visible water vapor or spring water. == Subordinate Shrines == [[File:Oomiwa-jinja (tochigishi) jingu.JPG|thumb|200px|Jingū: houses the aidadono (shared) deities of the main shrine]] There are 15 shrine buildings in total: {{div col}} * Jingū * Gokoku Jinja * Fukujin Jinja * Ōsugi Jinja * Soreisha * Samon Jinja * Umon Jinja {{div col end}} '''Muro no Yashima''' {{div col}} * Sengen Jinja * Futarayama Jinja * Tsukuba Jinja * Raiden Jinja * Katori Jinja * Kashima Jinja * Kumano Jinja * Tenman-gū {{div col end}} == Annual Festivals == * Gantan-sai (January 1st) * New Year’s Pilgrimage and Shinshun Kigan-sai (January) * Setsubun-sai and Tsuina-shiki (February 3rd) * Kinen-sai (February 25th) * Chinka-sai (Early March) * Spring Grand Festival (April 16th) - Includes yabusame (horseback archery) * Hatsu-uma-sai (on the first Uma day in May) * Ōharae (June 30th) * Yashima-sai (August 1st) * Ōsugi-sai, Kaze-matsuri (Mid-August) * Shichi-go-san visits (November 15th) * Autumn Grand Festival (Mikoshi Festival) (around November 18-24) == Cultural Properties == === Tochigi City Designated Intangible Folk Cultural Properties === * Kagura of Ōmiwa Jinja - designated May 19, 1964 * Hoko (Spear) Festival of Ōmiwa Jinja - designated May 19, 1964 === Historic Sites === * Tochigi City Designated Historic Site "Shimotsuke Sōja (Muro no Yashima)" - designated February 16, 1968 == Location == * Address: Sōja-chō 477, Tochigi City, Tochigi Prefecture == Access == * About 15 minutes’ walk from Yashū-Ōtsuka Station on the Tōbu Utsunomiya Line == Surrounding Area == * Shimotsuke Kokuchō Ruins approx. 2.8 km south == Notes == {{Note help}} {{reflist}} == References == * Shrine’s official pamphlet "Ōmiwa Jinja Gaiyō" * "Nihon Rekishi Chimei Taikei: Tochigi-ken no Chimei" (Heibonsha), entry for Ōmiwa Jinja == See Also == * [[Ōmiwa Jinja (Nara)]] (Sakurai City, Nara Prefecture) == External Links == * [http://www.kuranomachi.jp/spot/soja/omiwa/ Ōmiwa Jinja] (Tochigi City Tourism Association) * [http://kir579053.kir.jp/jinjyacyo/?p=538 Ōmiwa Jinja] (Tochigi Prefecture Jinja-chō) {{Shinto Navbox}} {{DEFAULTSORT:Oomiwa Jinja Tochigishi}} [[Category:Shinto shrines in Tochigi Prefecture]] [[Category:History of Tochigi City]] [[Category:Buildings and structures in Tochigi City]] [[Category:Shikinaisha in Shimotsuke Province]] [[Category:Former Prefectural shrines]] [[Category:Miwa shrines]] [[Category:Shimotsuke Province|Shrine0]] ==See Also== * [[Ichinomiya]] * [[Shimotsuke Province]] [[Ichinomiya]] ** [[Futarasan jinja]] ** [[Utsunomiya Futarayama Jinja]] ==References== {{reflist}} {{draft categories| [[Category:Sōja shrines]] [[Category:Sōja shrines]]{{Sōja shrines}}[[category:original pages]] [[Category:Ken-sha]] [[en:Ōmiwa Jinja (Shimotsuke)]][[Category:Shikinai Shosha]] [[Category:Miwa shrines]] [[Category:original pages]][[Category:original pages]] [[ja:大神神社 (栃木市)]] }} {{shinto shrines}} {{⚠️🚨COPIED from EverybodyWiki ❗❕⚠️😡😤Please respect Licence CC-BY-SA ❗}} {{Source Wikipedia}} {{Miwa and Yamato Faith}}

{{Distinguish|Omiwa Shrine}}{{draft}} {{Infobox religious building | religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]] | image = Oomiwa-jinja (tochigishi) torii.JPG | deity = all the deities of its province | type = [[Sōja (Shinto)|Sōja shrine]] }} {{ill|Ōmiwa Jinja (Shimotsuke)|lt=Ōmiwa Jinja|ja|大神神社 (栃木市)}} is a [[Sōja (Shinto)|Sōja shrine]]. It enshrines all the [[kami]] of the shrines in [[Shimotsuke Province]] Ichinomiya and Soja are not the same thing but were sometimes combinedhttps://archive.ph/wip/XtZfZ {{nihongo|'''Sōja'''|総社|}} is a type of [[Shinto shrine]] where the ''[[kami]]'' of a region are grouped together into a single sanctuary. This "region" may refer to a ''[[shōen]]'', village or geographic area, but is more generally referred to a whole [[Provinces of Japan|province]]. The term is also occasionally called "'''sōsha'''". The ''sōja'' are usually located near the [[kokufu|provincial capital]] established in the [[Nara period]] under then ''[[ritsuryō]]'' system, and can either be a newly created shrine, or a designation for an existing shrine. The "sōja" can also be the "[[ichinomiya]]" of the province, which themselves are of great ritual importance.{{cite book |last1=Herbert |first1=Jean |title=Shinto:At the Fountain-head of Japan |date=2011 |publisher=Routledge |isbn=978-0-415-59348-9 |page=105}} Whenever a new [[Kokushi (official)|kokushi]] was appointed by the central government to govern a province, it was necessary for him to visit all of the sanctuaries of his province in order to complete the rites necessary for ceremonial inauguration. Grouping the ''kami'' into one location near the capital of the province greatly facilitated this duty,{{cite book |last1=Bocking |first1=Brian |title=A Popular Dictionary of Shinto |date=2016 |publisher=Routledge |isbn=978-1138979079}} The first mention of "sōja" appeared in the [[Heian period]], in the diary of Taira no Tokinori, dated March 9, 1099 in reference to the province of [[Inaba]]. {{cite book |last1=Hardacre |first1=Helen |title=Shinto: A History |date=2016 |publisher=Oxford University Press |isbn=978-0190621711}} The name "Sōja" is also found in place names such as the city of [[Sōja, Okayama| Sōja]] in [[Okayama Prefecture]]. ==Japanese content== {{Infobox Shinto shrine | name = Ōmiwa Jinja (Oomiwa Shrine) | image = [[File:Oomiwa-jinja (tochigishi) torii.JPG|280px]]
Torii | caption = | map_type = Japan Tochigi | coordinates = {{Coord|36|24|21.30|N|139|46|55.76|E|region:JP-09_type:landmark|display=inline,title|name=Ōmiwa Jinja}} | location = Sōja-chō 477, {{ill|Tochigi (city)|ja|栃木市|lt=Tochigi City}}, {{ill|Tochigi Prefecture|ja|栃木県|lt=Tochigi Prefecture}} | deity = Yamato-Ōmononushi-Kushi-mikatama no Mikoto | type = Shikinaisha (small), a disputed identification (ronsha), Sōja of Shimotsuke Province, Former Prefectural Shrine | founded = (Trad.) 48th year of Emperor Sujin’s reign | festival = November 18–26 }} '''Ōmiwa Jinja''' (大神神社, also romanized as Oomiwa Jinja) is a {{ill|Shinto shrine|ja|神社}} located in Sōja-chō, {{ill|Tochigi (city)|ja|栃木市|lt=Tochigi City}}, {{ill|Tochigi Prefecture|ja|栃木県|lt=Tochigi Prefecture}}, Japan. It is a possible match (ronsha) for a "Shikinaisha" (small) recorded in historical texts, and is known as the Sōja (total shrine) of Shimotsuke Province. Under the modern shrine rank system of the Meiji era, it was classified as a Prefectural Shrine. Historically, it was also known by other names such as "Shimotsuke Sōja Daimyōjin," "Sōja Rokusho Daimyōjin," and "Muroyashima Sōja Daimyōjin." During the Ritsuryō era, the provincial capital (kokufu) was located about 2 km south of the shrine. Ōmiwa Jinja served as the sōja of that kokufu, and the local place name “Sōja” is derived from this shrine.{{Cite web |url=https://www.city.tochigi.lg.jp/uploaded/attachment/55689.pdf|title=Chapter 2: Historical Scenery of Tochigi City to be Maintained and Improved |website=Tochigi City|accessdate=2024-11-11|page=177}} The shrine is also known for the "Muro no Yashima" (Muro no Yashima) mentioned in Matsuo Bashō’s famous travelogue, the "Oku no Hosomichi." == Deities Enshrined == '''Principal Deity:''' * *Yamato-Ōmononushi-Kushi-mikatama no Mikoto* (倭大物主櫛𤭖玉命)According to the shrine's official literature. : In the "Izumo no Kuni no Miyatsuko Kamuyogoto," this refers to Ōmononushi no Kami. The deity is said to be an offshoot of the Ōmiwa Jinja (大神神社) in Sakurai City, Nara Prefecture. During Emperor Sujin’s reign, suffering from natural disasters and plagues, the emperor had a dream in which the deity Ōmononushi appeared and gave instructions. Following them, a man named Ootataneko performed rites at Mount Miwa, resulting in the cessation of calamities and epidemics. This story is recorded in the "Nihon Shoki." '''Additional Deities (Aiadono-matsuri):''' * Kono-hanasakuya-hime (木花咲耶姫命) * Ninigi no Mikoto (瓊々杵命), husband of Kono-hanasakuya-hime * Ōyamatsumi no Mikoto (大山祇命), father of Kono-hanasakuya-hime * Hikohohodemi no Mikoto (彦火々出見命), child of Kono-hanasakuya-hime == History == === Founding === According to shrine tradition, during Emperor Sujin's era, Prince Toyokiirihiko (豊城入彦命), while subjugating the eastern provinces, prayed for victory and peace of mind at a place known as "Muro no Yashima." He is said to have enshrined the great deity of Ōmiwa (from the capital at Isonokami in Yamato) at this site, establishing the shrine.Shrine’s official literature. === Historical Overview === The mid-Heian period text "Engishiki Jinmyōchō" lists a “Ōgami Jinja” in Tsuga District, Shimotsuke Province. One theory identifies Ōmiwa Jinja with that shrine, making it a "ronsha" (disputed match).Another candidate is Taihei-san Jinja in Hirai-chō, Tochigi City. In ancient times, provincial governors (kokushi) would visit all shrines in the province, starting with the ichinomiya. To streamline this, they established a sōja near the kokufu to collectively worship all regional deities. Ōmiwa Jinja is believed to have served as the sōja of Shimotsuke Province. About 2.8 km south, the ruins of the Shimotsuke Kokuchō (provincial government offices) have been excavated. During the rebellion of Taira no Masakado (Heian period), the shrine suffered damage. Fujiwara no Hidesato and others helped rebuild it, and until the Muromachi period, it had grand buildings. However, during the Sengoku period, the remnants of Minagawa Hiroteru’s forces barricaded themselves in the shrine. Hōjō Ujinao’s army set it on fire, resulting in destruction and decline. It was said that through contributions by Tokugawa Iemitsu, who donated 30 koku of land and 10,000 pine saplings, the shrine was rebuilt in 1682 (Tenna 2) to its current form. However, no historical documents prior to the Meiji era have been found that clearly refer to this shrine as “Ōmiwa (Ōmiwa)” or “Ōmiwa.” One theory suggests that a deity from Ōmiwa Jinja (Ōmiwa Jinja in Yamato) was worshiped at another location and later merged at the Sōja of Shimotsuke.On-site information board. After the Meiji Restoration, in Meiji 6 (1873), the shrine was ranked as a Gōsha (village shrine) under the modern shrine ranking system. In Meiji 40 (1907), it was designated a shrine entitled to government offerings (Shinsen Heihaku Ryō Kyōshin Jinja), and in Meiji 44 (1911), it was promoted to Prefectural Shrine. Major renovations took place in 1924 (Taishō 13) and 1993 (Heisei 5). The Kuniho family traditionally served as hereditary Ōmiya-gūji (chief priests). === Shinhonors (Shinkai)=== * On August 29, Genkei 4 (880), it was elevated from Junior Fifth Rank, Lower Grade to Senior Fifth Rank, Upper Grade in the "Nihon Sandai Jitsuroku." The recorded deity name is "Miwa no Kami (三和神)"—some believe this refers to this shrine."Tochigi-ken no Chimei" (Heibonsha) entry on Ōmiwa Jinja. == Precincts == === Shrine Buildings === File:Oomiwa-jinja (tochigishi) honden.JPG|Honden File:Oomiwa-jinja (tochigishi) haiden.JPG|Haiden File:Oomiwa-jinja (tochigishi) kaguraden.JPG|Kagura-den === Sanctuary Forest === The forested area around Ōmiwa Jinja is designated as the Sōja Greenery Conservation Area by Tochigi Prefecture.{{Cite web |url=https://www.pref.tochigi.lg.jp/d04/30jikannti/12souja.html|title=12 Sōja Greenery Environmental Conservation Area|website=Tochigi Prefecture|accessdate=2024-11-11}} === Muro no Yashima === [[File:Oomiwa-jinja (tochigishi) muronoyashima.JPG|thumb|200px|Muro no Yashima]] [[File:TochigiOhmiwaShine2.JPG|thumb|200px|Bashō’s haiku monument before Muro no Yashima]] "Muro no Yashima" has long been known as a utamakura (poetic place name) in classical Japanese poetry. The island in the shrine’s pond is said to be its location (though some argue this is a later association).See Kōjien, "Muro no Yashima." (Kotobank [https://kotobank.jp/word/%E5%AE%A4%E3%81%AE%E5%85%AB%E5%B3%B6-642624 article]) It has been mentioned since the Nara period and appears in anthologies like the "Man’yōshū" and "Kokin Wakashū." Famous poems: * Fujiwara no Sanekata (Shika Wakashū) * Minamoto no Shigeyuki’s daughter (Zoku Goshūi Wakashū) * Ōe no Masafusa (Shinshūi Wakashū) * Fujiwara no Shunzei (Chōshū Eiso) * Fujiwara no Teika (Shin Chokusen Wakashū) Meanings associated with Muro no Yashima: * A site of a myth where Konohanasakuya-hime proved her chastity by setting herself aflame inside a room. * Possibly relates to a hearth’s smoke, turning into metaphorical love’s burning flame. * The marshy Omoigawa River basin producing water vapor or rising mist. * Over time associated with passionate love, smoke, and even kagerō (heat haze or spider’s thread). Matsuo Bashō and his companion Sora mention Muro no Yashima in "Oku no Hosomichi," but they did not include a haiku in the main text. However, in Sora’s “Haikai Kakinotame,” one of Bashō’s verses “ito asobi ni musubitsukitaru keburi kana” ("Oh, the smoke that has tied itself to the thread playing in the air!") is recorded. This haiku is inscribed on a monument erected in 1869 (Meiji 2) by the late Edo period haijin Kōun Kaku Shunpō, with calligraphy by Hagiwara Shūgan, an Edo-period calligrapher.{{Cite web |title=Tochigi Inishie no Kairō: History of Cultural Properties |url=https://www.inishie.tochigi.jp/detail.html?course_id=5&id=0|accessdate=2024-02-22}} Today’s Muro no Yashima is about 800 tsubo (approx. 2,640 square meters) of landscaped garden featuring eight small islands with small shrines dedicated to various prominent deities, including Tsukuba, Tenman, Kashima, Raiden, Sengen, Kumano, Futarayama, and Katori. There is no visible water vapor or spring water. == Subordinate Shrines == [[File:Oomiwa-jinja (tochigishi) jingu.JPG|thumb|200px|Jingū: houses the aidadono (shared) deities of the main shrine]] There are 15 shrine buildings in total: {{div col}} * Jingū * Gokoku Jinja * Fukujin Jinja * Ōsugi Jinja * Soreisha * Samon Jinja * Umon Jinja {{div col end}} '''Muro no Yashima''' {{div col}} * Sengen Jinja * Futarayama Jinja * Tsukuba Jinja * Raiden Jinja * Katori Jinja * Kashima Jinja * Kumano Jinja * Tenman-gū {{div col end}} == Annual Festivals == * Gantan-sai (January 1st) * New Year’s Pilgrimage and Shinshun Kigan-sai (January) * Setsubun-sai and Tsuina-shiki (February 3rd) * Kinen-sai (February 25th) * Chinka-sai (Early March) * Spring Grand Festival (April 16th) - Includes yabusame (horseback archery) * Hatsu-uma-sai (on the first Uma day in May) * Ōharae (June 30th) * Yashima-sai (August 1st) * Ōsugi-sai, Kaze-matsuri (Mid-August) * Shichi-go-san visits (November 15th) * Autumn Grand Festival (Mikoshi Festival) (around November 18-24) == Cultural Properties == === Tochigi City Designated Intangible Folk Cultural Properties === * Kagura of Ōmiwa Jinja - designated May 19, 1964 * Hoko (Spear) Festival of Ōmiwa Jinja - designated May 19, 1964 === Historic Sites === * Tochigi City Designated Historic Site "Shimotsuke Sōja (Muro no Yashima)" - designated February 16, 1968 == Location == * Address: Sōja-chō 477, Tochigi City, Tochigi Prefecture == Access == * About 15 minutes’ walk from Yashū-Ōtsuka Station on the Tōbu Utsunomiya Line == Surrounding Area == * Shimotsuke Kokuchō Ruins approx. 2.8 km south == Notes == {{Note help}} {{reflist}} == References == * Shrine’s official pamphlet "Ōmiwa Jinja Gaiyō" * "Nihon Rekishi Chimei Taikei: Tochigi-ken no Chimei" (Heibonsha), entry for Ōmiwa Jinja == See Also == * [[Ōmiwa Jinja (Nara)]] (Sakurai City, Nara Prefecture) == External Links == * [http://www.kuranomachi.jp/spot/soja/omiwa/ Ōmiwa Jinja] (Tochigi City Tourism Association) * [http://kir579053.kir.jp/jinjyacyo/?p=538 Ōmiwa Jinja] (Tochigi Prefecture Jinja-chō) {{Shinto Navbox}} {{DEFAULTSORT:Oomiwa Jinja Tochigishi}} [[Category:Shinto shrines in Tochigi Prefecture]] [[Category:History of Tochigi City]] [[Category:Buildings and structures in Tochigi City]] [[Category:Shikinaisha in Shimotsuke Province]] [[Category:Former Prefectural shrines]] [[Category:Miwa shrines]] [[Category:Shimotsuke Province|Shrine0]] ==See Also== * [[Ichinomiya]] * [[Shimotsuke Province]] [[Ichinomiya]] ** [[Futarasan jinja]] ** [[Utsunomiya Futarayama Jinja]] ==References== {{reflist}} {{draft categories| [[Category:Sōja shrines]] [[Category:Ken-sha]] [[en:Ōmiwa Jinja (Shimotsuke)]][[Category:Shikinai Shosha]] [[Category:Miwa shrines]] [[Category:original pages]][[Category:original pages]] [[ja:大神神社 (栃木市)]] }} {{shinto shrines}} {{⚠️🚨COPIED from EverybodyWiki ❗❕⚠️😡😤Please respect Licence CC-BY-SA ❗}} {{Source Wikipedia}} {{Miwa and Yamato Faith}}
